newsitem.title: LEBANON: Israeli-backed militiaman wounded in south Lebanon.
newsitem.headline: Israeli-backed militiaman wounded in south Lebanon.

text.p: Moslem guerrillas shelled two posts of Israel's client militia in south Lebanon on Thursday, wounding one militiaman, militia sources said.

The South Lebanon Army (SLA) militiaman was wounded when guerrillas fired mortar bombs at an SLA post at Toumat Jezzine in an area officially outside Israel's south Lebanon occupation zone but under Israeli control, the SLA sources said.
Other guerrillas fired mortar bombs at a second militia position at Shqeef an-Naml in the western flank of the border zone but no one was hurt, the sources added.
In retaliation, Israeli and SLA artillery gunners fired shells into guerrilla-held areas outside the 15-km (nine-miles)-deep border strip.
The pro-Iranian Hizbollah claimed responsibility for the Toumat Jezzine attack.
Hizbollah (Party of God) leads a guerrilla war on Israeli and SLA forces in a bid to oust them from the south Lebanon zone set up in 1985 to prevent cross-border raids on northern Israel.
